pr_title: Fixes FF daily data with different data/exchange tz
pr_body:
The issue with having a different data and exchange time zone is that
daily data no longer follows a common assumption of beginning and ending
at midnight each day. This assumption was baked into the existing impl
to its own detriment. Specifically, the get next market open date calc
was being improperly executed. In most case (data resolution < one day)
we would use the start time of the bar, but since daily data spans a day,
we need to use the end time of the bar to properly calculate this value.

Fixes #1073
pr_comments:
@jaredbroad @andrewhart098 @StefanoRaggi 

Comments very welcome. This is super sensitive code. The commit message describes my
line of thinking as to why this happened and also the reason for the fix. In short, with daily
data being filled forward on daily increments, we need to choose a different reference
start time in order to properly calculate next market open.

Also, please check the test added as it is a modified form of #1073 because I think the
assertions outlined there were incorrect as they were missing the Sat-Sun bar, since the
market opens at 5PM `America/New_York` and the daily bar ends at 8PM same tz.

@mchandschuh - I think this PR fixes at least one bug in the `FillForwardEnumerator`. I have a hunch that there's still another bug somewhere in the FFE.  When running an algorithm using Oanda daily data, the consolidators are sporadically updated (if at all).

I'm struggling to place my finger on it exactly, but basically in the main AlgorithmManager loop, at the point where the AlgorithmManager updates the consolidators, [there's a conditional](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/eeb3e55696885e0db36cbfba45710182fb96b42b/Engine/AlgorithmManager.cs#L478) that ensures that data is only passed into the consolidator if it has the same Date as `Algorithm.UtcTime`. Even with this PR, virtually all of the data in `ConsolidatorUpdateData` is one day behind  `Algorithm.UtcTime`.

My hunch is that it's the FFE, but I'm still digging.  This PR does affect how the consolidators are updating. For now, I'm going to leave this PR open until I understand why the Oanda daily consolidators are not updating. It could be something else too! There's a lot of code between the AlgorithmManager and the FFE.

Thanks for looking into this. If you have any idea why the Oanda daily data consolidators are not updating I'd love to hear it.

yes, this is a similar bug as the other one addressed. The real issue is anytime we do 'daily' rounding on data with different data/exchange time zones. Daily data with different data/exchange time zones will be timestamped at, for example, 1600, so the daily rounding drastically changes the value.

Really what we're trying to do here is determine if it's a fill forwarded piece of data from a lower resolution, such as daily data fill forwarding every minute. In this case, we don't want to push the duplicate data through. I suppose the correct solution here would be to round in the data time zone.

I have some code working locally that performs the rounding in the data time zone. I'm trying to find other cases where this might be an issue as well, should have this PR updated this afternoon.
fyi, first commit includes whitespace changes, easier to view diff commit by commit

The rounding must be performed in the data time zone. That extension method
converts to data tz, performs rounding, and then converts it back.

There is definitely something wrong with the existing impl, which is what I
get for playing around with it too much. I've been beyond swamped this past
week, but hoping to take another look at it soon.

If you have time feel free to modify this PR. My thought process here is
that rounding must be performed in the data time zone. Consider daily
rounding, which will always end up at midnight. But then consider data time
zone != exchange time zone. Daily rounding should be rounded to midnight in
the data time zone, not the exchange time zone.

I did a little analysis and also identify consolidators as needing some
attention as they perform a similar check. Basically the logical check that
is usually being performed is to check if a piece of data is on the
requested resolution of not. For example, daily data will fill forward on
minutes, but you don't want daily bars pumped into consolidators every
minute.

Feel free to call and chat and I hope to get back to this issue soon.
@andrewhart098 - noticed `CustomDataRegressionAlgorithm` is failing when I run on master, is this normal?
Newest implementation lazily evaluates the bar end times and pre sorts based on fill forward/data resolution values

@jaredbroad - still need to get some benchmark numbers on old vs new -- was able to run through the daily oanda case and the data is getting pumped through as expected -- not a huge fan of the rounding we do in `SubscriptionSynchronizer` -- basically the FFE can emit something on say an hour 0900-100 and if it's daily data, it would round that down to the previous day before being pumped into the algo

@jaredbroad - this is about as good as it gets without unrolling the enumerable into a giant if/else block.

This implementation is ~40% slower than the existing, but is still only about a second slower over 2.7 million fill forward bars.

#### Existing
```

DataPoints : 2765521
```

#### New
```

DataPoints : 2765521
```


I think this is ready for a final review.

issue_context.title: FillForwardEnumerator enumerating Oanda daily data incorrectly
comments: @andrewhart098 - I'll take a deeper look this evening. Thanks for providing a test that reproduces the issue
@andrewhart098 - just a comment on the tests. `Assert.AreEqual(expected, actual)` -- in your test it appears you have these arguments flipped.

@andrewhart098 - I'm also questioning your expected results. Since the market opens at 5pm on Sunday, I believe we need to create a fillforward bar for Saturday 2000 to Sunday 2000, like below:

```
Thursday 7/19/2012 8:00:00 PM - Friday 7/20/2012 8:00:00 PM
Saturday 7/21/2012 8:00:00 PM - Sunday 7/22/2012 8:00:00 PM
Sunday   7/22/2012 8:00:00 PM - Monday 7/23/2012 8:00:00 PM
```

Please confirm. I've identified a bug which basically drops the offset from daily data on weekend which resulted in bars at midnight instead of 8PM as expected.

review_comments:
I'm not 100% sure how this works but: During an execution, if this is true once, wouldn't it be true always for that data source? or can it change?
If you can trust it will return always the same, maybe there could be some type of cache/memory of previous checks, to avoid calling RoundDownInTimeZone for each data.
the date time value here will be different for every data point so we can't cache the value
